keyTakeaways: Gujarati New Year 2027 (Bestu Varas) is Saturday 30 October; the Pratipada tithi runs from 7:05 PM on Friday 29 October to 5:51 PM on Saturday, New Delhi time.
It opens Gujarati Vikram Samvat 2084; from 1 January to Diwali night the same calendar reads 2083, which is why 2027 Gujarati calendars say 2083–2084.
North India's Chaitra-based Vikram year reached 2084 on Wednesday 7 April 2027, nearly seven months before Gujarat.
Bestu comes from બેસવું, 'to sit', not English 'best'; a 1901 Gazetteer calls salt (sabras) the luckiest purchase of the Kartik new year day.
48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so a Saal Mubarak link should read well on a small screen.

faqs.question: Is Gujarati New Year on 29 or 30 October in 2027?
faqs.answer: Saturday 30 October 2027. The Kartik Shukla Pratipada tithi begins at 7:05 PM on Friday 29 October (New Delhi time), but a panchang day is counted from sunrise, so the new year is the Saturday. Friday 29 October is Diwali and Lakshmi Puja.

faqs.question: What year is it in the Gujarati calendar after Diwali 2027?
faqs.answer: Vikram Samvat 2084. From 1 January to Diwali night on 29 October 2027 the Gujarati calendar reads Samvat 2083; it turns to 2084 at Bestu Varas on Saturday 30 October 2027.

faqs.question: Why do Gujarat and North India start the Vikram year in different months?
faqs.answer: They use the same era but different new-year days. Gujarat begins the year on Kartik Shukla Pratipada, the day after Diwali, while North India begins it on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada in spring, which fell on Wednesday 7 April 2027. Both calendars reach 2084 in 2027, about seven months apart.

faqs.question: How do I convert a Vikram Samvat year to an English year?
faqs.answer: For the Gujarati calendar, subtract 56 for dates from January up to Diwali and 57 for dates from Bestu Varas to 31 December. So Samvat 2084 runs from 30 October 2027 to Diwali 2028. The Vikram era is counted from 57 BCE.

faqs.question: Does Bestu Varas mean 'best day'?
faqs.answer: No. Bestu is બેસતું (besatũ), a participle of the Gujarati verb બેસવું, 'to sit', and varas means 'year'. Read literally it is the year that sits down or settles in; it has nothing to do with the English word 'best'.

faqs.question: Why do Gujarati families buy salt on New Year morning?
faqs.answer: The Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency (1901, p. 349) records that salt, called mithu or sabras, 'the essence of taste', was the luckiest purchase on the Kartik new year day. Sabras is still listed as a Gujarati word for salt. The record is from 1901, so whether a family keeps it today varies.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Saal Mubarak and Nutan Varshabhinandan?
faqs.answer: Both mean happy new year. સાલ મુબારક (sāl mubārak) pairs 'year' with the Persian-derived 'blessed', and is the everyday greeting; નૂતન વર્ષાભિનંદન (nūtan varṣābhinandan) is built from Sanskrit words for 'new', 'year' and 'greeting' and reads more formal, which suits clients and elders.

faqs.question: When was Gujarati New Year in 2026?
faqs.answer: Tuesday 10 November 2026, opening Samvat 2083. Diwali 2026 fell on Sunday 8 November, and because the Pratipada began only at 12:31 PM on Monday 9 November, Monday was a gap day between the two.

faqs.question: When are Bhai Beej and Labh Pancham in 2027?
faqs.answer: Bhai Beej, the Gujarati Bhai Dooj, is Sunday 31 October 2027, the day after Bestu Varas. Labh Pancham, the bright fifth of Kartik, is Wednesday 3 November 2027.

faqs.question: Is it too early to say Saal Mubarak on Diwali morning?
faqs.answer: By the Gujarati count, yes: on the morning of Friday 29 October 2027 the old year still has a day to run. The new-year tithi begins at 7:05 PM that evening, so from Lakshmi Puja night onwards a Saal Mubarak is on time.

faqs.question: Can I send someone a Saal Mubarak page on SubhSandesh?
faqs.answer: There is no Bestu Varas template. SubhSandesh's interactive Diwali card at subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali works on any date, so you can write a Saal Mubarak into its diya wishes and sealed letter, but its scenes are Diwali ones, ending on a Shubh Deepavali card. For a partner, the Rewind template looks back on your year together.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Gujarati New Year 2027: Saturday 30 October, Vikram Samvat 2084

Gujarati New Year 2027, Bestu Varas, falls on **Saturday 30 October 2027**, the morning after Diwali, and it opens **Vikram Samvat 2084** in the Gujarati count. [Drik Panchang's Gujarati New Year 2027 page](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/gujarati-newyear/gujarati-newyear-date-time.html?year=2027) gives the Kartik Shukla Pratipada tithi from 7:05 PM on Friday 29 October to 5:51 PM on Saturday 30 October, New Delhi time. A panchang day starts at sunrise, so Saturday is the day.

If your Saal Mubarak goes out as a link, write it for a phone: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on one. Expect to write it late, too. In our nearest festival data, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89 pages, a different festival), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the festival day itself and 27.0% the day before.

## Gujarati New Year 2027 date: Saturday 30 October, with no gap day

Bestu Varas 2027 shares its Saturday with Govardhan Puja and Annakut. The Pratipada begins at 7:05 PM on Friday, after the Lakshmi Puja lamps are lit, so Friday night still belongs to the old year and Saturday's sunrise opens the new one. One search-engine AI summary we saw on 22 October 2026 read the tithi's Friday start as the festival date and answered "Friday 29 October"; the panchang itself says Saturday.

The two years do not line up the same way. Diwali 2026 is Sunday 8 November, but [Drik Panchang's 2026 page](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/gujarati-newyear/gujarati-newyear-date-time.html?year=2026) puts Gujarati New Year on Tuesday 10 November 2026, opening Samvat 2083, because that Pratipada begins only at 12:31 PM on Monday 9 November. Monday is a gap day in 2026; in 2027 the new year follows Diwali directly.

## Vikram Samvat 2084, and why a 2027 calendar also says 2083

The Vikram era counts from 57 BCE, so its year number runs about 57 ahead of the common era. Igor Kotin's [2023 survey of Indian calendars](https://journals.urfu.ru/index.php/uos/article/view/9364), in the peer-reviewed Ural Survey of Oriental Studies, gives that start and makes the wider point that Indian calendars differ on when both the year and the era begin. Gujarat starts its Vikram year on Kartik Shukla Pratipada, the day after Diwali; North India starts the same era in spring, on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada.

So a Gujarati calendar for 2027 carries two numbers. From 1 January to Diwali night it is Samvat 2083, and from Saturday 30 October it is 2084, which is why Gujarati calendars for the year are titled "2083–2084". The working rule: add 56 to the year from January until Diwali, and 57 from Bestu Varas to 31 December.

North India reached 2084 first. Chaitra Shukla Pratipada fell on Wednesday 7 April 2027, the day [Drik Panchang lists Gudi Padwa](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/gudi-padwa/gudi-padwa-date-time.html?year=2027) and the start of Shaka 1949. Kotin puts the Shaka era about 78 years after the common era, so Shaka 1949 plus 135 gives the same Vikram 2084, nearly seven months before Gujarat gets there.

| Calendar | New year in 2027 | Year number from that day | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gujarati Vikram Samvat (begins in Kartik) | Saturday 30 October | 2084 | Drik Panchang, 2027 |
| North Indian Vikram Samvat (begins in Chaitra) | Wednesday 7 April | 2084 | Drik Panchang; Shaka + 135 |
| Marathi and Kannada Shaka (Gudi Padwa, Ugadi) | Wednesday 7 April | 1949 | Drik Panchang, 2027 |
| Indian national calendar (Shaka era) | Monday 22 March | 1949 | Kotin 2023: year starts 22 March |

A business letter dated "Kartik sud 1, Samvat 2084" therefore means 30 October 2027, while a Hindi wedding card printed with "Samvat 2084" in June 2027 is not a mistake. Both are right in their own reckoning.

## What "Bestu Varas" means, and what it does not

Bestu Varas is Gujarati બેસતું વરસ (besatũ varas), also written બેસતું વર્ષ (besatũ varṣ). બેસતું is a participle of the verb [બેસવું (besvũ), which Wiktionary defines as "to sit"](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%AA%AC%E0%AB%87%E0%AA%B8%E0%AA%B5%E0%AB%81%E0%AA%82), and વરસ and વર્ષ both mean "year". Read literally, it is the year that sits down, the year settling into place.

That literal reading is our gloss; we found no dictionary entry that spells the idiom out. What the dictionary does rule out is English "best". At least one ranking calendar page, checked on 22 October 2026, translates Bestu Varas as "best day", and nothing in the verb supports that.

The two greetings come from different languages. સાલ મુબારક (sāl mubārak) pairs સાલ, "year", with મુબારક, from Persian, "blessed" or "happy", while નૂતન વર્ષાભિનંદન (nūtan varṣābhinandan) is Sanskrit-built: નૂતન, "new", વર્ષ, "year", and abhinandana, which Monier-Williams glosses as "delighting, praising, applauding".

## Bestu Varas customs, from sabras salt to Labh Pancham

The oldest detailed record we found is the [Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, Vol. IX Part I, Gujarat Population: Hindus (1901)](https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.113147), page 349. It says salt, called mithu, "the sweetener", and sabras, "the essence of taste", is "the luckiest of all purchases on the new year day in Kartik". The same page records the other side of salt's power: a dying person gave salt to Brahmans, so most high-caste Hindus took care not to pass it from hand to hand.

The word survives. Wiktionary's Gujarati entry for મીઠું (mīṭhũ), salt, still lists સબરસ (sabras) as a synonym, so the first errand of Saturday 30 October can be a small packet of it. The Gazetteer is a 1901 record, not a survey of today, so ask an elder whether your family kept it.

The rest of the morning is familiar from the top calendar pages we read on 22 October 2026: new clothes, an early temple visit, and a round of calls on elders. Bhai Beej, the Gujarati Bhai Dooj, follows on Sunday 31 October 2027. Labh Pancham, the bright fifth of Kartik, falls on Wednesday 3 November 2027 and closes the first stretch of the new year.

## Saal Mubarak lines in Gujarati script, with transliteration

Each line below opens in Gujarati script, then gives the transliteration and the English. They are written for this post; change the names and send.

- For grandparents: "સાલ મુબારક (sāl mubārak), happy new year, Ba and Bapuji. Every Samvat has started at your door, and 2084 will too."
- For a client or supplier: "નૂતન વર્ષાભિનંદન (nūtan varṣābhinandan), new-year greetings. Thank you for your trust through Samvat 2083; here is to an honest, busy 2084."
- For a family WhatsApp group: "નૂતન વર્ષની શુભેચ્છાઓ (nūtan varṣnī śubhecchāo), good wishes for the new year, from our kitchen to every one of yours."
- For a friend: "Sāl mubārak! First sabras of the year bought, first message of the year sent. Your turn."
- For a husband or wife: "સાલ મુબારક (sāl mubārak). Same seat beside you on every Bestu Varas morning, Samvat 2084 included."
- For a child: "નવું વરસ (navũ varas), a new year! One new thing to learn, one old toy to give away."
- For someone in Canada or the US: "Your Saturday has not started yet, but in Ahmedabad Samvat 2084 already has. Sāl mubārak for when you wake."
- For a card or Story: "સાલ મુબારક · વિક્રમ સંવત ૨૦૮૪ (sāl mubārak, vikram saṃvat 2084)"

The script lines use only words we checked in a dictionary. If you write longer Gujarati, have a fluent speaker read it before you send, because Gujarati verbs and adjectives change form with gender.

## When to send a Saal Mubarak: from 7:05 PM Friday to Saturday morning

The Pratipada begins at 7:05 PM on Friday 29 October 2027, so a message after Lakshmi Puja is already a new-year greeting by the panchang. Saturday morning suits elders, because Bestu Varas is a visiting day and a phone call before the house fills up lands better than a text at noon.

Late is not wrong. In the Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, 11.2% of the 89 pages were built after the festival had passed, and a Saal Mubarak sent on Sunday still reaches someone in the first days of Samvat 2084. The one hard edge is Diwali itself: sent on Friday morning, a Saal Mubarak arrives a year early by the Gujarati count.

## Sending one Saal Mubarak page, and where SubhSandesh falls short

For one person who deserves more than a line, SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card, where they light a diya waiting at their door and a row of wish diyas](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) can carry a Bestu Varas message, because the page works on any date. Choose family, love or friend mode, write your Saal Mubarak into the diya wishes and into the letter sealed in a red-and-gold shagun liffafa, add up to six photos to the sky lanterns, and send the private link. It opens in any browser without an app, and you can add a password, which 38.5% of creators across the platform set before sharing.

Be clear about the fit. It is a Diwali card: it has diyas, rangoli, a sparkler and a mithai box that opens onto a Shubh Deepavali card, and no New Year, Samvat or sabras scene. It is a one-person greeting, not a group broadcast, and for Ba and Bapuji a morning visit still counts for more than any link.

For a partner, there is a different idea. The Gujarati year closes on Diwali night, so a look back fits better than a wish forward: [Rewind turns your year together into a story they tap through](https://subhsandesh.in/rewind). It is a couples template, not a festival page, and it carries no Gujarati or Diwali theme.
